'''Christopher Ike Anigbogu''' (born October 17, 1998) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Vanoli Cremona]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA). He played [[college basketball]] for one season with the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]]. As a freshman, he was a key reserve for a Bruins squad that advanced to the Sweet 16 of the [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. After the season, Anigbogu was selected by the [[Indiana Pacers]] in the second round of the [[2017 NBA draft]] with the 47th overall pick. He played two seasons for the Pacers.

==Early life==
Anigbogu was born in [[San Diego, California]], to Nigerian parents Chris and Veronica Anigbogu.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ike Anigbogu|website=UCLABruins.com|url=http://www.uclabruins.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4743|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170408155817/http://www.uclabruins.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4743|archive-date=April 8, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> He attended [[Temescal Canyon High School (Lake Elsinore, California)|Temescal Canyon High]] in [[Lake Elsinore, California|Lake Elsinore]] as a freshman and played on their [[junior varsity team]].<ref name=fowler_03152017>{{cite news|last=Fowler|first=Clay|title=How UCLA built its best roster since Kevin Love joined Russell Westbrook|date=March 15, 2017|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20170315/how-ucla-built-its-best-roster-since-kevin-love-joined-russell-westbrook|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170410050944/http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20170315/how-ucla-built-its-best-roster-since-kevin-love-joined-russell-westbrook|archive-date=April 10, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> The following year, he transferred to [[Centennial High School (Corona, California)|Centennial High]] in [[Corona, California|Corona]], where he was also enrolled in the [[International Baccalaureate]] program.<ref name=whicker_03052017/> A skinny, {{convert|6|ft|7|in|adj=on}} sophomore, he averaged two [[point (basketball)|points]] and 2.5 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] per game as the Huskies advanced to the state finals.<ref name=fowler_03152017/>

As a junior in 2015, Anigbogu led the team to the state regional finals, where the Huskies lost to [[Chino Hills High School|Chino Hills]], who were led by [[Lonzo Ball]].<ref name=whicker_03052017>{{cite news|last=Whicker |first=Mark |title=UCLA freshman Ike Anigbogu is the last line of defense |date=March 5, 2017 |newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News |url=http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20170305/whicker-ucla-freshman-ike-anigbogu-is-the-last-line-of-defense |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170409112549/http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20170305/whicker-ucla-freshman-ike-anigbogu-is-the-last-line-of-defense |archive-date=April 9, 2017 |url-status=live }}</ref> In his senior year, he was limited by injuries and a family emergency.<ref name=pareneti_04162016>{{cite news|last=Pareneti |first=Jeffrey |title=ALL-AREA BOYS BASKETBALL: All-Inland first-team selections |date=April 16, 2016 |newspaper=The Press-Enterprise |url=https://www.pressenterprise.com/2016/04/16/all-area-boys-basketball-all-inland-first-team-selections/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170409111840/http://www.pe.com/articles/first-800145-team-players.html |archive-date=April 9, 2017 |url-status=live }}</ref> Anigbogu took three weeks off to attend an uncle's funeral in Nigeria.<ref>{{cite news|last=Zink |first=David |title=Huskies Anigbogu learns lesson in appreciation during trip to Nigeria |date=January 12, 2016 |newspaper=The Press-Enterprise |url=https://www.pressenterprise.com/2016/01/12/zink-huskies-anigbogu-learns-lesson-in-appreciation-during-trip-to-nigeria/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170409113158/http://www.pe.com/articles/anigbogu-791533-basketball-family.html |archive-date=April 9, 2017 |url-status=live }}</ref> During the playoffs, he was limited by an injured knee. For the season, the Huskies were 20–5 when Anigbogu played. He finished with averages of 19 points, 11 rebounds and 3 [[block (basketball)|blocks]].<ref name=pareneti_04162016/>

==College career==
Ranked nationally as a consensus top-50 [[college recruiting|recruit]], Anigbogu attended the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA), where he was part of a Bruins freshmen class that included more heralded five-star players like Ball and [[T. J. Leaf]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Hines |first=Travis |title=UCLA freshman to miss 4-6 weeks with knee injury |date=October 25, 2016 |work=College Basketball Talk |url=http://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2016/10/25/ucla-freshman-to-miss-4-6-weeks-with-knee-injury/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170409111222/http://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2016/10/25/ucla-freshman-to-miss-4-6-weeks-with-knee-injury/ |archive-date=April 9, 2017 |url-status=live }}</ref>  Anigbogu and Leaf had played on the same [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) team, the Compton Magic, who had also been coached by UCLA assistant [[David Grace (basketball)|David Grace]].<ref name=fowler_03152017/> The newcomers were expected to help turn around a program that [[2015–16 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|a year earlier]] had suffered its fourth losing season in the previous 68 years.<ref name=fowler_03252017>{{cite news|last=Fowler|first=Clay|title=Thrilling ride made UCLA basketball's season-ending loss sting|date=March 25, 2017|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20170325/thrilling-ride-made-ucla-basketballs-season-ending-loss-sting|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170411074719/http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20170325/thrilling-ride-made-ucla-basketballs-season-ending-loss-sting|archive-date=April 11, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Indiana Pacers (2017–2019)===
Working out for the [[Indiana Pacers]] in his fourth pre-draft tryout, Anigbogu twisted his right knee, which precluded him from participating in any further workouts leading up to the draft.<ref name=taylor_06282017>{{cite news|last=Taylor|first=Nate|title=Pacers see potential rewards in drafting Ike Anigbogu, Edmond Sumner|date=June 28, 2017|newspaper=Indianapolis Star|url=http://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2017/06/28/pacers-see-potential-rewards-drafting-anigbogu-sumner/433373001/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201023063445/https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2017/06/28/pacers-see-potential-rewards-drafting-anigbogu-sumner/433373001/|archive-date=October 23, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> His draft stock fell over concerns about his knee, and the Pacers selected him in the second round with the 47th overall pick. He was joined in Indiana by UCLA teammate Leaf, who the Pacers had selected in the first round.<ref>{{cite news|last=Botemps|first=Tim|title=The biggest winners and losers from the 2017 NBA draft|date=June 23, 2017|newspaper=The Washington Post|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/sports/wp/2017/06/23/the-biggest-winners-and-losers-from-the-2017-nba-draft/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170711232035/https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/sports/wp/2017/06/23/the-biggest-winners-and-losers-from-the-2017-nba-draft/|archive-date=July 11, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> Anigbogu had surgery to repair [[cartilage]] in his knee and missed the [[NBA Summer League]] while rehabbing.<ref name=taylor_06282017/><ref name=michael_09242018/><ref>{{cite news|last=Montieth|first=Mark|title=Second-Round Picks Will Need Time to Heal|date=June 28, 2017|website=Pacers.com|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/second-round-picks-will-need-time-heal|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170906094205/http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/second-round-picks-will-need-time-heal|archive-date=September 6, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref>  He made his NBA debut on October 20, 2017, playing two minutes in a 114–96 loss to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20171020/PORIND#/boxscore |title=Archived copy |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2017-10-21 |archive-date=2017-10-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171021115504/http://www.nba.com/games/20171020/PORIND#/boxscore |url-status=dead }}</ref> At just 19 years old, he was the youngest player in the NBA in [[2017–18 Indiana Pacers season|2017–18]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Hotchkiss|first=Wheat|title=The Fort Report: Anigbogu, Mad Ants Sweep Pair of Home Games|date=January 10, 2018|website=Pacers.com|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/fort-report-anigbogu-mad-ants-sweep-pair-home-games|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180308102830/http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/fort-report-anigbogu-mad-ants-sweep-pair-home-games|archive-date=March 8, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> In his first season, he played 11 games with the Pacers,<ref name=nba_02072019/> and had multiple [[assignment (NBA G League)|assignments]] to their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Pacers Recall Anigbogu|date=November 21, 2017|website=NBA.com|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-recall-anigbogu|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171126052929/http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-recall-anigbogu|archive-date=November 26, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/assignments/|title=2018-19 NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=November 9, 2018}}</ref>

During the offseason, Anigbogu missed his second straight summer league after undergoing minor surgery on his knee.<ref name=michael_09242018>{{cite news|last=Michael|first=J.|title=After another knee procedure, Ike Anigbogu feels optimistic about 2nd season with Pacers|date=September 24, 2018|newspaper=Indianapolis Star|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2018/09/24/indiana-pacers-ike-anigbogu-knee-feels-optimistic-2nd-season/1407044002/|access-date=February 10, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite tweet|user=Pacers|author=Indiana Pacers|number=1013494360850223105|date=July 1, 2018|title=Ike Anigbogu had minor surgery on his leg, which is keeping him out of Summer League this year. "We're just taking it day by day, step by step."|access-date=February 10, 2019}}</ref>
He played just three games for the Pacers in [[2018–19 Indiana Pacers season|2018–19]] before they waived him to complete a deal at the NBA trade deadline on February 7, 2019.<ref name=nba_02072019>{{cite web|title=Pacers Waive Anigbogu|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-waive-anigbogu|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 7, 2019|date=February 7, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Glaspie|first=Akeem|title=Pacers receive high grades for Wes Matthews signing|date=February 8, 2019|newspaper=Indianapolis Star|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2019/02/08/nba-trade-deadline-pacers-moves-receive-high-marks/2810786002/|access-date=February 10, 2019}}</ref> He had spent most of his time in the G League and was playing well, averaging 11.1 points, 9.5 rebounds and 1.9 blocks in 21 games with Fort Wayne. However, he missed several games due to knee soreness.<ref>{{cite news|title=Anigbogu recalled from Fort Wayne but won't play Thursday|date=February 7, 2019|work=Fox Sports Indiana|url=https://www.foxsports.com/indiana/story/indiana-pacers-recall-ike-anigbogu-from-fort-wayne-mad-ants-of-nba-g-league-020619|access-date=February 8, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Agness|first=Scott|title=Pacers acquire second-round pick at deadline, plan to add veteran Wesley Matthews|date=February 7, 2019|work=The Athletic|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/805937/2019/02/07/pacers-acquire-second-round-pick-at-deadline-plan-to-add-veteran-wesley-matthews/|access-date=February 10, 2019|url-access=subscription |quote=Anigbogu, who has played just six minutes this season, has spent most of his time in Fort Wayne with the Mad Ants and sat out several games due to knee soreness.}}</ref>

===Erie BayHawks (2020–2021)===
On January 31, 2020, the [[Erie BayHawks (2019–)|Erie BayHawks]]—the G League affiliate of the [[New Orleans Pelicans]]—acquired Anigbogu off waivers.<ref>{{cite news|title=BayHawks Acquire Ike Anigbogu|url=https://erie.gleague.nba.com/news/bayhawks-acquire-ike-anigbogu|date=January 31, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 31, 2020|archive-date=February 3, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200203014949/https://erie.gleague.nba.com/news/bayhawks-acquire-ike-anigbogu/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He played six games and averaged 9.5 points and 4.8 rebounds.<ref name=nba_12022020>{{cite news|title=Pelicans sign four players|date=December 2, 2020|website=NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-four-players|access-date=December 3, 2020}}</ref>

Anigbogu signed with New Orleans in December 2020,<ref name=nba_12022020/> but he was waived after the preseason.<ref>{{cite web|title=Pelicans waive four|date=December 19, 2020|website=NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-waive-four|access-date=December 20, 2020}}</ref> He rejoined the BayHawks for the 2020–21 G League season, scheduled to be played in a bubble in [[Orlando, Florida]], due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Erie BayHawks' preseason roster includes 3 returnees for NBA G League season|date=June 13, 2021|newspaper=Erie Times-News|url=https://www.goerie.com/story/sports/nba/2021/01/12/erie-bayhawks-announce-preseason-roster-nba-g-league-season/6646684002/|access-date=January 16, 2021}}</ref> On March 1, he was waived after suffering a season-ending injury.<ref>{{cite news|title=NBA G League Transactions|work=NBA.com|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210306044025/https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|access-date=March 6, 2021|archive-date=2021-03-06}}</ref>

===Birmingham Squadron (2022; 2024–present)===
On January 20, 2022, Anigbogu was acquired via returning player rights by the [[Birmingham Squadron]].<ref name="202122GLTrans">{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021-22 NBA G League Transactions|access-date=March 31, 2022}}</ref> However, he was waived on February 28 after suffering a season-ending injury.<ref name="202122GLTrans" />

On January 12, 2024, Aninogbu returned to the Squadron.<ref>{{cite web|title=Birmingham Squadron Sign Ike Anigbogu|url=https://birmingham.gleague.nba.com/news/birmingham-squadron-sign-ike-anigbogu|website=NBA.com|date=January 12, 2024|access-date=January 12, 2024}}</ref>

===Vanoli Cremona (2025–present)===
On July 6, 2025, he signed with [[Vanoli Cremona]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.afrobasket.com/Nigeria/news/945591/Cremona-lands-Ike-Anigbogu|title=Cremona lands Ike Anigbogu|last=|first=|date=July 6, 2025|website=|publisher=Afrobasket|language=En|access-date=August 31, 2025}}</ref>
